revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Puzzle Problem
revealWordProblem.text: Before a sale, a toy store's puzzle stock was 25% 300-piece puzzles, 15% 500-piece puzzles, and the rest 1,000-piece puzzles. During the sale the store sold ALL of its 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles — 120 puzzles in all. How many of each type did the store have before the sale?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The 120 puzzles sold were the 300-piece and 500-piece stock together, which is 25% + 15% = 40% of the whole stock. So 120 is the part and 40% is the percent: 0.4t = 120, giving t = 120 ÷ 0.4 = 300 puzzles in total. Now take each percent of that whole: 300-piece = 0.25 × 300 = 75, 500-piece = 0.15 × 300 = 45, and 1,000-piece = 0.6 × 300 = 180. Check: 75 + 45 = 120 sold ✓ and 75 + 45 + 180 = 300 total ✓.

launch.narrative: Every percent problem has three pieces: the part, the whole, and the percent. So far the whole has always been handed to you. Today it is the missing piece — a sale price without the original price, a car's current value without its sticker price. Your job is to work backwards to the whole.

conceptIntro.heading: Working backwards to the whole
conceptIntro.intro: When you know a part and the percent it represents, the whole is what is missing. A double number line, a ratio table, or an equation will each get you there — the equation is the fastest once you trust it.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Percent × whole = part. When the whole is unknown, divide the part by the percent in decimal form: whole = part ÷ decimal.

iDo.title: Watch me find the original price of the sweater
lines: Akela paid $42 for a sweater on sale, and that was 60% of the original price. The $42 is the part; the original price is the whole, which is 100%.
On a double number line, I put $42 under 60%. To find a smaller step, I use 10%: if 60% is $42, then 10% is 42 ÷ 6 = $7.
Now I count up to the whole: 100% is ten of those 10% steps, so 10 × $7 = $70.
The equation says the same thing in one move: 0.6 × v = 42, so v = 42 ÷ 0.6 = 70. The original price was $70 — larger than the sale price, which is exactly what a discount should mean.

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: Sheng's car is now worth $26,600, which is 70% of what his parents paid for it. Find the original price.
Name the pieces first: $26,600 is the part, 70% is the percent, and the purchase price is the unknown whole.
Write the percentage statement as an equation, using the decimal form: 0.7v = 26,600.
Solve by dividing both sides by 0.7: v = 26,600 ÷ 0.7 = 38,000. The car cost $38,000 when they bought it.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake when finding the whole is multiplying by the percent instead of dividing. For "$42 is 60% of the original price," computing 0.6 × 42 = $25.20 makes the original price SMALLER than the sale price — impossible for a discount. Since percent × whole = part, the whole is found by dividing: 42 ÷ 0.6 = $70. Whenever the percent is less than 100%, the whole must come out larger than the part, so a smaller answer is the tell.
